summary: JetBrains' landing page for JetBrains Mono, a free coding font: a dark, all-monospace page that types its own headline (with an editable last word), lists six key features with giant numerals, then argues each design decision (taller x-height, code-specific ovals, cut strokes, 9° italic, ligatures) with animated SVG diagrams, a draggable 13px comparison against Consolas and on/off ligature switches, before a weight-tabbed glyph set, 148 languages, install steps, OFL licence FAQ and credits. A teal terminal-style cookie dialog covers the centre of every screen capture.

instances.look: Fixed dark bar on every screen: JetBrains logo, small-caps anchors INTRO · KEY FEATURES · DESIGN · FONT FAMILY at left, 'How to install', 'License' and a blue 'Download font' pill at right (collapses to a hamburger on mobile)
instances.ux: Anchor links scroll to sections; Download font links straight to the zip
instances.learn: A permanent download button in the nav is enough checkout for a free font

reconstruction.layout: Fixed 72px bar, 1240px container, links 24px apart, button right
reconstruction.typography: ~11px JetBrains Mono caps tracked for anchors; ~12px for right links; button ~12px white on blue

instances.look: Four lines of grey monospace at ~100px, 'JetBrains / Mono. / A typeface / for developers_', ending in a blinking underscore cursor; under it a small version block (v2.304, Updated 1,372 days ago, Release notes ↗), a big blue 'Download font' button and 'It's free & open source'
instances.ux: The headline types itself on letter by letter (typed.js) on load; the last word 'developers' is contenteditable, so visitors can retype it
instances.learn: Type the pitch like a shell prompt and leave the last word editable: the hero becomes the first tester without any UI
